target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosures D023 and D150 both describe Intel's competitive landscape in the data center and cloud markets, specifically highlighting competitors like AMD, NVIDIA, and the risk of customers (cloud providers/OEMs) developing custom silicon. The 2024 disclosure D118 covers the same specific topic: intensified competition from these same entities (AMD, NVIDIA, Qualcomm) and internally developed semiconductors by OEMs and cloud providers, driven by AI trends. The evidence shows a direct thematic correspondence regarding the sources of competitive pressure.

peer_results.rationale: The provided AMD candidates (amd_2024_7_D002 and amd_2024_7_D003) focus on AMD's internal strategic actions (consolidating AI teams, acquiring Silo AI, and acquiring ZT Systems) rather than discussing the competitive landscape, customer vertical integration, or market demand risks in a manner comparable to Intel's risk factor disclosures. Intel's Item 7 section describes external competitive pressures and market dynamics, whereas AMD's selected disclosures describe internal execution and M&A activities.

comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for products has been and is likely to continue to be affected by factors including customer loss, economic conditions, AI-related demand, distributor inventory, technology adoption rates, the shift to cloud-based solutions, and order timing.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Avago explicitly identify AI-related demand as a key driver affecting their business performance in 2024. Intel highlights the 'high demand for AI-related products and services' as intensifying its competitive environment, noting that the proliferation of AI is a primary factor in the changing landscape. Avago similarly lists 'anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products' as a specific factor affecting product demand, alongside technology adoption rates. While Intel focuses on the competitive pressure and ecosystem shifts (such as ARM adoption) driven by this demand, Avago focuses on the demand-side variables and inventory dynamics, but both confirm AI demand as a central business driver/risk factor for the fiscal year.

sentences.text: Our competitive environment has intensified in recent years, and we expect it to continue to do so in the future, including as a result of the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products and services.
• anticipated or actual demand for AI-related products;

comparisons.peer_summary: The company experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins in 2024, driven by increased demand growth partly from AI deployment, normal customer inventories, and industry supply discipline.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron identify AI deployment as a significant catalyst for market conditions in 2024, though they frame it differently based on their respective positions in the semiconductor value chain. Intel cites the 'proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products' as intensifying its competitive landscape. Micron states that 'increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI' contributed to substantial improvements in pricing and margins. Both disclosures attribute positive market momentum or competitive intensity specifically to the AI trend, confirming it as a shared industry-wide business driver for the fiscal year.

sentences.text: Our competitive environment has intensified in recent years, and we expect it to continue to do so in the future, including as a result of the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products and services.

Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Demand estimates for new use cases and services like DGX Cloud and generative AI may be incorrect, creating revenue volatility. While recent generative AI models have increased data center demand, their long-term trajectory remains unknown, and the company may not generate significant revenue from these new areas.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA address the uncertainty and volatility associated with the rapid emergence of new AI use cases in 2024. Intel notes that the competitive environment has intensified due to the 'proliferation of AI,' implying a fast-changing and unpredictable landscape. NVIDIA explicitly warns that 'demand estimates for new use cases... can be incorrect and create volatility,' and while generative AI has increased demand, its 'long-term trajectory is unknown.' Both disclosures highlight the challenge of managing business strategy and competition in an environment where AI adoption is accelerating but its long-term stability is still being defined.

sentences.text: Our competitive environment has intensified in recent years, and we expect it to continue to do so in the future, including as a result of the proliferation of AI and high demand for AI-related products and services.

Our demand estimates for new use cases, applications, and services can be incorrect and create volatility in our revenue or supply levels, and we may not be able to generate significant revenue from these use cases, applications, and services.
Recent technologies, such as generative AI models, have emerged, and while they have driven increased demand for Data Center, the long-term trajectory is unknown.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm expects continued intense competition, partly driven by vertical integration by certain customers, such as Apple.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm identify competition from vertically integrated customers, specifically Apple, as a key competitive pressure. Intel explicitly states that it 'face[s] increasing competition from Apple's products and ecosystem' which utilizes internally developed ARM-based semiconductors. Qualcomm similarly highlights 'continued intense competition, including from vertical integration by certain of our customers (e.g., Apple).' While Intel focuses on the loss of client CPU designs, and Qualcomm focuses on the broader strategic threat of customer vertical integration, both disclosures cite Apple's move to in-house silicon as a significant competitive risk and business driver.

sentences.text: For example, in 2020, Apple introduced PC products utilizing its own internally developed ARM-based semiconductor designs in place of our client CPUs, and we face increasing competition from Apple's products and ecosystem.
• We expect continued intense competition, including from vertical integration by certain of our customers (e.g., Apple).
